thread:
anna: Quick sync — ran a small canary of deploy-time warmers on staging this morning. Posting a short perf summary + a proposed rollout plan.

anna: TL;DR: prefix cache hit rate up, p50 gen latency down ~18%, but we saw a regression for long-seq workloads and some KV-eviction thrash. Need feedback on safe throttling + scheduling.

anna: Measurements (staging, model: redwood-7b-v1, 4 GPUs):
- before: prefix-hit 12% avg, p50 210ms, tokens/sec 480
- warmers on: prefix-hit 68% avg, p50 172ms, tokens/sec 560
- but: 32k token tail tests p95 increased 14% and KV-evict logs spike during concurrent prewarm + user traffic

anna: Profiling notes: kernel selection shifted to more small-batch kernels during warmup bursts (we saw many kernel switches at 10ms granularity), causing additional kernel launch overhead. Batching heuristics also converted to smaller effective batches under our synthetic pattern.

sam: Nice lift on p50. Do you have hit-rate by prefix length?

anna: Yes — heatmap attached (summarized):
- short prefixes (<=8 tokens): hit 82%
- medium (9-64): hit 71%
- long (65-512): hit 23%
So warmers strongly help short/medium prompts.

sam: Makes sense. For long prefixes we probably shouldn't prewarm with full long sequences — they pollute KV and cause eviction.

mike: Question: how are you keying the cache? current keying is model_id + prefix_hash + temp_zone ?

anna: Current canary key = model_id + body_prefix_sha1( first N tokens ) + quant_profile_tag. We intentionally avoid request ids. Using first N=64 for the canary.

zara: Might be worth trying two-tier keying: short-prefix key (first 16 tokens) for warmers and full-prefix key in production. Warmers then populate the small-key fast-path without filling the full KV for long sequences.

mike: Agree. Also throttle the synthetic concurrency. In the canary we sent bursts of 50 concurrent warmers and that likely caused kernel churn. Limit to 2 warmers/GPU and interleave with real traffic.

anna: Good call. I also observed kernel-selection flipflop: during warmers the runtime preferred kernel A for small batch, but when user traffic returned it switched to fused kernel B and that switch had a cost. We should avoid immediate oscillation.

zara: We can add a short kernel-stability window: prefer current kernel for N seconds after a high-load event. Low risk change.

sam: For autoscaling events — plan? When new instances spin up we lose warm state. Proposal: run a targeted prewarm job on scale-up that sequentially warms hot prefixes with low concurrency.

anna: Proposed rollout (safe):
1) Opt-in canary on staging: warmers use short-prefix (16 tokens), concurrency cap 2/GPU, rate limit 10 reqs/min per instance.
2) Add kernel-stability window to runtime (30s prefer current kernel).
3) Add scale-up hook: on new node ready -> run <warm-job> (see script).
4) Schedule low-priority nightly job to warm common prefixes across capacity buckets.

anna: Warmup curl script (used in canary):
```bash
# warm-prefix.sh
PREFIX=\"Hello, my name\"
for i in $(seq 1 40); do
  curl -s -X POST \"https://staging.api.redwood.ai/v1/generate\" \
    -H 'Authorization: Bearer $WARM_KEY' \
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -d '{"model":"redwood-7b-v1","input":"'$PREFIX'","max_tokens":8}' &
  sleep 0.5
done
wait
```

anna: k8s job snippet we ran (low priority, node-affinity to new nodes):
```yaml
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata:
  name: prewarm-common-prefixes
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      affinity:
        nodeAffinity: { .. match newly created node labels .. }
      containers:
      - name: warmer
        image: warmers:latest
        args: ["/bin/warm-prefix.sh"]
      restartPolicy: Never
  backoffLimit: 2
```

deploy-bot: Deploy 1753002200 started for staging/redwood-7b-v1 (includes warmers canary).

infra-bot: CronJob prewarm-nightly scheduled at 03:00 UTC (slot: low-priority).

sam: Two operational notes: (1) we need metrics for KV fill rate + eviction_count per shard during warm. (2) add a warm-tag metric so we can attribute cost to warmers vs user traffic.

anna: Agree. I added a temporary counter warm_prefill_requests and warm_prefill_tokens in staging prometheus. Will open dashboard.

mike: Also watch quantized-kernel state transitions — when we hit a quant profile tag mismatch runtime may recompile kernels causing pauses. Warmers should include quant_profile_tag to avoid that.

zara: For regression we saw in long-seq p95: hypothesis is eviction thrash + kernel-switch stalls. Two mitigations: restrict warmers to short keys, and increase KV capacity for pinned model shards during deploys. That latter is heavier ops.

anna: Action items:
- [anna] update canary script to use 16-token key and cap concurrency (ETA: today)
- [sam] add eviction_count + warm-tag metrics (ETA: tomorrow)
- [mike] prototype kernel-stability window in runtime (ETA: next week)
- [zara] draft scale-up hook job with node-affinity and slow ramp (ETA: this Fri)

zara: One more thought — autoscaler spike warmers: when scaling from 1->N, run warmers staggered across N over 5 minutes so not all nodes prefill same shards simultaneously.

anna: Perfect. I'll run a second canary with these constraints later today and post updated numbers.

mike: If the second canary still shows p95 regressions we should snapshot KV and kernel logs and run a replay.

anna: Will do. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: Deploy 1753003600 completed (staging).

anna: Second canary started (1753003800). Low concurrency, short-key warmers. Will report by end of day.

infra-bot: Note: scheduled warm-job created: job/prewarm-staging-1753003800 (ttl 1d).

anna: Update: after constraints, prefix-hit stable ~64%, p50 down 16%, long-seq p95 regression reduced to +3%. KV-evict spikes no longer observed. Still need kernel-stability change to avoid oscillation.

sam: Great progress. Let's iterate on kernel window and then promote to limited production rollout behind a feature flag.

anna: Sounds good. I'll open PRs for the scripts + feature flags and link here.

mike: Thanks — also add a guard in warmers to detect perf inverted (if p50 increases >5% during warm, auto-scale down warmers).

anna: Added to action items. Closing thread after PRs linked.
